# Overview

This document contains the complete solution to Section I (Items 1 to 3).
Each item includes the code, example output, and a brief interpretation.

| Item | Topic |
|------|-------|
| 1 | Probability that a randomly selected product is defective |
| 2 | Front end for univariate and bivariate discrete random variables |
| 3 | Simulation of searches until a key phrase is found |

Requirements: R >= 4.0. The Shiny app in Item 2 also needs `install.packages("shiny")`.

---

# Item 1: Probability that a product is defective

**Method.** Factory *i* produces a proportion $x_i$ of the product ($\sum x_i = 1$,
$0.10 \le x_i \le 0.40$) with defective rate $y_i$ ($\sum y_i = 0.12$, $0.01 \le y_i \le 0.05$).
By the law of total probability

$$P(D) = \sum_{i=1}^{3} P(D \mid F_i)P(F_i) = \sum_{i=1}^{3} x_i y_i,
\qquad P(F_i \mid D) = \frac{x_i y_i}{P(D)}.$$

## Validation and calculation functions

```{r item1-functions}
# Parse "0.2, 0.3 0.5" or "20%, 30%, 50%" into proportions
parse_probs <- function(txt) {
  parts <- strsplit(trimws(txt), "[,;[:space:]]+")[[1]]
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  is_pct <- grepl("%", parts, fixed = TRUE)
  vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("%", "", parts, fixed = TRUE)))
  vals[is_pct] <- vals[is_pct] / 100
  vals
}

# Returns "" if valid, otherwise a message explaining the problem
validate_vector <- function(v, lo, hi, total, n = 3) {
  if (length(v) != n || any(is.na(v))) return(sprintf("Enter exactly %d numeric values.", n))
  if (any(v < lo - TOL | v > hi + TOL)) return(sprintf("Every value must lie in [%g, %g].", lo, hi))
  if (abs(sum(v) - total) > TOL) return(sprintf("Values sum to %.6f but must sum to %g.", sum(v), total))
  ""
}

# Core calculation
defect_probability <- function(x, y) {
  joint <- x * y
  p_def <- sum(joint)
  list(p_defective = p_def, joint = joint, posterior = joint / p_def)
}
```

## Interactive prompt version

This function asks the user for the inputs and repeats the prompt until they are valid.
It is not run when knitting. Call `run_item1_interactive()` in the console.

```{r item1-interactive, eval=FALSE}
ask_vector <- function(label, symbol, lo, hi, total) {
  repeat {
    cat(sprintf("\nEnter the 3 %s values (%s1, %s2, %s3), each in [%g, %g], summing to %g:\n",
                label, symbol, symbol, symbol, lo, hi, total))
    v <- parse_probs(readline("> "))
    msg <- validate_vector(v, lo, hi, total)
    if (msg == "") return(v)
    cat("  [Invalid]", msg, "\n")
  }
}

run_item1_interactive <- function() {
  x <- ask_vector("production proportion", "x", 0.10, 0.40, 1)
  y <- ask_vector("defective rate", "y", 0.01, 0.05, 0.12)
  res <- defect_probability(x, y)
  print(data.frame(Factory = paste("Factory", 1:3), x = x, y = y,
                   `x*y` = res$joint, `P(F|D)` = round(res$posterior, 4), check.names = FALSE))
  cat(sprintf("\nP(defective) = %.6f\n", res$p_defective))
}
run_item1_interactive()
```

## Demonstration

Validation of invalid inputs:

```{r item1-validation}
tests <- list(
  "x out of range (0.50, 0.30, 0.20)" = list(parse_probs("0.50, 0.30, 0.20"), 0.10, 0.40, 1),
  "x does not sum to 1 (0.2, 0.3, 0.4)" = list(parse_probs("0.2, 0.3, 0.4"), 0.10, 0.40, 1),
  "y out of range (0.06, 0.03, 0.03)"   = list(parse_probs("0.06, 0.03, 0.03"), 0.01, 0.05, 0.12),
  "y does not sum to 0.12 (1%, 2%, 3%)"  = list(parse_probs("1%, 2%, 3%"), 0.01, 0.05, 0.12),
  "valid x (25%, 35%, 40%)"             = list(parse_probs("25%, 35%, 40%"), 0.10, 0.40, 1)
)
for (nm in names(tests)) {
  t <- tests[[nm]]
  msg <- validate_vector(t[[1]], t[[2]], t[[3]], t[[4]])
  cat(sprintf("%-40s -> %s\n", nm, ifelse(msg == "", "VALID", msg)))
}
```

Example calculation with valid inputs $x = (0.25, 0.35, 0.40)$ and $y = (0.03, 0.04, 0.05)$:

```{r item1-example}
x <- c(0.25, 0.35, 0.40)
y <- c(0.03, 0.04, 0.05)
stopifnot(validate_vector(x, 0.10, 0.40, 1) == "", validate_vector(y, 0.01, 0.05, 0.12) == "")
res <- defect_probability(x, y)

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Factory = paste("Factory", 1:3),
  `Proportion x` = x, `Defect rate y` = y,
  `x * y` = res$joint,
  `P(Factory | Defect)` = round(res$posterior, 4),
  check.names = FALSE
))
cat(sprintf("P(defective) = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", res$p_defective, 100 * res$p_defective))
```

**Interpretation.** The overall defect rate is a weighted average of the factory defect
rates, with production shares as weights. Factory 3 makes 40% of the output but accounts for
about 48% of the defective items, because it has both the largest share and the highest
defect rate.

# Item 2: Front end for discrete random variables

## Helper functions

All calculations and validity checks used by the app are defined here so they can also be
demonstrated in this document.

```{r item2-helpers}
parse_nums <- function(txt) {
  parts <- strsplit(trimws(txt), "[,;[:space:]]+")[[1]]
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(parts))
  if (length(parts) == 0 || any(is.na(v))) stop("Please enter numeric values only (separated by commas or spaces).")
  v
}

check_probs <- function(p, label = "Probabilities") {
  if (any(p < 0 | p > 1)) stop(sprintf("%s must all lie in [0, 1].", label))
  if (abs(sum(p) - 1) > 1e-6) stop(sprintf("%s must sum to 1 (they currently sum to %.6f).", label, sum(p)))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

make_pmf <- function(x, p, label = "Probabilities") {
  if (length(x) != length(p)) stop(sprintf("Number of values (%d) and probabilities (%d) differ.", length(x), length(p)))
  if (anyDuplicated(x)) stop("Values must be distinct.")
  check_probs(p, label)
  o <- order(x)
  list(x = x[o], p = p[o])
}

pmf_stats <- function(d) {
  m <- sum(d$x * d$p)
  v <- sum((d$x - m)^2 * d$p)
  list(mean = m, var = v, sd = sqrt(v))
}

plot_pmf <- function(d, main) {
  plot(d$x, d$p, type = "h", lwd = 4, col = "steelblue", ylim = c(0, max(d$p) * 1.1),
       xlab = "x", ylab = "P(X = x)", main = main)
  points(d$x, d$p, pch = 16, col = "steelblue")
}

plot_cdf <- function(d, main) {
  plot(stepfun(d$x, c(0, cumsum(d$p))), verticals = FALSE, pch = 16, col = "firebrick",
       xlim = range(d$x) + c(-1, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "x", ylab = "F(x)", main = main)
}

# Joint table: one row per line (rows = X values), columns = Y values
parse_joint <- function(txt, nx, ny) {
  lines <- strsplit(trimws(txt), "\n")[[1]]
  lines <- lines[nzchar(trimws(lines))]
  rows <- lapply(lines, parse_nums)
  if (length(rows) != nx) stop(sprintf("Joint table needs %d rows; found %d.", nx, length(rows)))
  if (any(vapply(rows, length, 1L) != ny)) stop(sprintf("Every row needs %d entries.", ny))
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

# Build the full bivariate object: joint, marginals
make_bivariate <- function(x, y, J) {
  if (anyDuplicated(x) || anyDuplicated(y)) stop("X values must be distinct, and Y values must be distinct.")
  check_probs(as.vector(J), "Joint probabilities")
  ox <- order(x); oy <- order(y)
  x <- x[ox]; y <- y[oy]; J <- J[ox, oy, drop = FALSE]
  dimnames(J) <- list(paste0("x=", x), paste0("y=", y))
  list(x = x, y = y, J = J, mx = list(x = x, p = rowSums(J)), my = list(x = y, p = colSums(J)))
}

# Conditional distribution of X | Y = v  (type "XgY")  or  Y | X = v  (type "YgX")
conditional <- function(b, type, v) {
  if (type == "XgY") {
    j <- match(v, b$y); if (is.na(j)) stop("Conditioning value not found among Y values.")
    if (b$my$p[j] == 0) stop("P(Y = y) = 0, conditional distribution undefined.")
    list(dist = list(x = b$x, p = b$J[, j] / b$my$p[j]), lab = sprintf("X | Y = %g", v))
  } else {
    i <- match(v, b$x); if (is.na(i)) stop("Conditioning value not found among X values.")
    if (b$mx$p[i] == 0) stop("P(X = x) = 0, conditional distribution undefined.")
    list(dist = list(x = b$y, p = b$J[i, ] / b$mx$p[i]), lab = sprintf("Y | X = %g", v))
  }
}
```

## Demonstration: validity checks

```{r item2-validation}
try_it <- function(expr) tryCatch({ force(expr); "VALID" }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))

cat("Probability 1.2 in list      :", try_it(make_pmf(1:3, c(1.2, -0.1, -0.1))), "\n")
cat("Probabilities sum to 0.9     :", try_it(make_pmf(1:3, c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3))), "\n")
cat("Length mismatch              :", try_it(make_pmf(1:3, c(0.5, 0.5))), "\n")
cat("Non-numeric input            :", try_it(parse_nums("1, two, 3")), "\n")
cat("Valid input                  :", try_it(make_pmf(1:4, c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4))), "\n")
```

## Demonstration: univariate distribution

```{r item2-univariate, fig.height=4}
d <- make_pmf(parse_nums("1, 2, 3, 4"), parse_nums("0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4"))
s <- pmf_stats(d)
knitr::kable(data.frame(x = d$x, `P(X=x)` = d$p, `F(x)` = cumsum(d$p), check.names = FALSE))
cat(sprintf("Mean = %.4f, Variance = %.4f, SD = %.4f\n", s$mean, s$var, s$sd))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot_pmf(d, "PDF (probability mass function)")
plot_cdf(d, "CDF")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Demonstration: bivariate distribution

```{r item2-bivariate}
x <- parse_nums("0, 1, 2")
y <- parse_nums("0, 1")
J <- parse_joint("0.10, 0.20\n0.15, 0.25\n0.20, 0.10", length(x), length(y))
b <- make_bivariate(x, y, J)

cat("Joint distribution:\n"); print(b$J)
cat("\nMarginal of X:\n"); print(data.frame(x = b$mx$x, p = b$mx$p))
cat("\nMarginal of Y:\n"); print(data.frame(y = b$my$x, p = b$my$p))

sx <- pmf_stats(b$mx); sy <- pmf_stats(b$my)
cat(sprintf("\nX: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f\nY: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f\n",
            sx$mean, sx$var, sy$mean, sy$var))
```

```{r item2-biv-plots, fig.height=7}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot_pmf(b$mx, "Marginal PDF of X"); plot_cdf(b$mx, "Marginal CDF of X")
plot_pmf(b$my, "Marginal PDF of Y"); plot_cdf(b$my, "Marginal CDF of Y")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y = 1$:

```{r item2-conditional, fig.height=4}
cd <- conditional(b, "XgY", 1)
sc <- pmf_stats(cd$dist)
print(data.frame(x = cd$dist$x, `P(X=x|Y=1)` = cd$dist$p, check.names = FALSE))
cat(sprintf("%s: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f\n", cd$lab, sc$mean, sc$var))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot_pmf(cd$dist, paste("Conditional PDF:", cd$lab))
plot_cdf(cd$dist, paste("Conditional CDF:", cd$lab))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## The interactive Shiny front end

The code below builds the app using the helper functions above. It is not run when knitting.
To launch it, run the chunk interactively in RStudio (after running the helper chunk), or
copy the code to `app.R` together with the helper functions and call `shiny::runApp()`.

```{r item2-shiny, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Discrete Random Variable Calculator"),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Univariate",
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          textInput("u_x", "Values of X (comma separated)", "1, 2, 3, 4"),
          textInput("u_p", "Probabilities (comma separated)", "0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4"),
          helpText("Each probability must be in [0, 1] and they must sum to 1.")
        ),
        mainPanel(
          verbatimTextOutput("u_err"), tableOutput("u_table"), verbatimTextOutput("u_stats"),
          fluidRow(column(6, plotOutput("u_pdf")), column(6, plotOutput("u_cdf")))
        )
      )),
    tabPanel("Bivariate",
      sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
          textInput("b_x", "Values of X (rows)", "0, 1, 2"),
          textInput("b_y", "Values of Y (columns)", "0, 1"),
          textAreaInput("b_joint", "Joint probabilities (one row per X value)",
                        "0.10, 0.20\n0.15, 0.25\n0.20, 0.10", rows = 6),
          uiOutput("cond_controls")
        ),
        mainPanel(
          verbatimTextOutput("b_err"),
          h4("Joint distribution"), tableOutput("b_joint_tbl"),
          h4("Marginal distributions"),
          fluidRow(column(6, tableOutput("b_mx")), column(6, tableOutput("b_my"))),
          verbatimTextOutput("b_stats"),
          fluidRow(column(6, plotOutput("bx_pdf")), column(6, plotOutput("bx_cdf"))),
          fluidRow(column(6, plotOutput("by_pdf")), column(6, plotOutput("by_cdf"))),
          h4("Conditional distribution"), tableOutput("b_cond_tbl"), verbatimTextOutput("b_cond_stats"),
          fluidRow(column(6, plotOutput("c_pdf")), column(6, plotOutput("c_cdf")))
        )
      ))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  bad <- function(e) structure(list(msg = conditionMessage(e)), class = "bad")

  # ---- univariate ----
  u_dist <- reactive(tryCatch(make_pmf(parse_nums(input$u_x), parse_nums(input$u_p)), error = bad))
  u_ok <- function() !inherits(u_dist(), "bad")
  output$u_err <- renderText({ d <- u_dist(); if (inherits(d, "bad")) paste("Input error:", d$msg) else "" })
  output$u_table <- renderTable({ req(u_ok()); d <- u_dist()
    data.frame(x = d$x, `P(X=x)` = d$p, `F(x)` = cumsum(d$p), check.names = FALSE) })
  output$u_stats <- renderText({ req(u_ok()); s <- pmf_stats(u_dist())
    sprintf("Mean E[X] = %.4f\nVariance Var(X) = %.4f\nStd. deviation = %.4f", s$mean, s$var, s$sd) })
  output$u_pdf <- renderPlot({ req(u_ok()); plot_pmf(u_dist(), "PDF") })
  output$u_cdf <- renderPlot({ req(u_ok()); plot_cdf(u_dist(), "CDF") })

  # ---- bivariate ----
  b_data <- reactive(tryCatch({
    x <- parse_nums(input$b_x); y <- parse_nums(input$b_y)
    make_bivariate(x, y, parse_joint(input$b_joint, length(x), length(y)))
  }, error = bad))
  b_ok <- function() !inherits(b_data(), "bad")
  output$b_err <- renderText({ d <- b_data(); if (inherits(d, "bad")) paste("Input error:", d$msg) else "" })

  output$cond_controls <- renderUI({
    req(b_ok())
    tagList(
      radioButtons("cond_type", "Conditional distribution of:",
                   c("X given Y = y" = "XgY", "Y given X = x" = "YgX")),
      selectInput("cond_val", "Conditioning value", choices = b_data()$y))
  })
  observeEvent(input$cond_type, {
    req(b_ok()); d <- b_data()
    updateSelectInput(session, "cond_val", choices = if (input$cond_type == "XgY") d$y else d$x)
  })

  output$b_joint_tbl <- renderTable({ req(b_ok()); b_data()$J }, rownames = TRUE, digits = 4)
  output$b_mx <- renderTable({ req(b_ok()); d <- b_data()$mx; data.frame(x = d$x, `P(X=x)` = d$p, check.names = FALSE) })
  output$b_my <- renderTable({ req(b_ok()); d <- b_data()$my; data.frame(y = d$x, `P(Y=y)` = d$p, check.names = FALSE) })
  output$b_stats <- renderText({ req(b_ok()); d <- b_data(); sx <- pmf_stats(d$mx); sy <- pmf_stats(d$my)
    sprintf("X: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f\nY: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f", sx$mean, sx$var, sy$mean, sy$var) })
  output$bx_pdf <- renderPlot({ req(b_ok()); plot_pmf(b_data()$mx, "Marginal PDF of X") })
  output$bx_cdf <- renderPlot({ req(b_ok()); plot_cdf(b_data()$mx, "Marginal CDF of X") })
  output$by_pdf <- renderPlot({ req(b_ok()); plot_pmf(b_data()$my, "Marginal PDF of Y") })
  output$by_cdf <- renderPlot({ req(b_ok()); plot_cdf(b_data()$my, "Marginal CDF of Y") })

  cond_dist <- reactive({
    req(b_ok(), input$cond_val, input$cond_type)
    res <- tryCatch(conditional(b_data(), input$cond_type, as.numeric(input$cond_val)), error = bad)
    validate(need(!inherits(res, "bad"), if (inherits(res, "bad")) res$msg else ""))
    res
  })
  output$b_cond_tbl <- renderTable({ cd <- cond_dist()
    data.frame(value = cd$dist$x, probability = cd$dist$p, cumulative = cumsum(cd$dist$p)) })
  output$b_cond_stats <- renderText({ cd <- cond_dist(); s <- pmf_stats(cd$dist)
    sprintf("%s: mean = %.4f, variance = %.4f", cd$lab, s$mean, s$var) })
  output$c_pdf <- renderPlot({ cd <- cond_dist(); plot_pmf(cd$dist, paste("Conditional PDF:", cd$lab)) })
  output$c_cdf <- renderPlot({ cd <- cond_dist(); plot_cdf(cd$dist, paste("Conditional CDF:", cd$lab)) })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

**Interpretation.** For the univariate example, $E[X] = 3$ and $Var(X) = 1$, and the CDF
rises in steps of size equal to each probability until it reaches 1. In the bivariate example the
marginals are obtained by summing the joint table over the other variable, and the conditional
distribution is a column (or row) of the joint table rescaled by its marginal probability so that
it sums to 1. If X and Y were independent, every conditional distribution of X would equal its
marginal; comparing the output above shows whether that holds here.

---

# Item 3: Search simulation

Each site contains the key phrase with probability `p` (set in the YAML `params`, default
`r params$p`). Let $X$ be the number of searches up to and including the first success, so
$X \sim \text{Geometric}(p)$ with $P(X=k) = (1-p)^{k-1}p$, $E[X] = 1/p$ and $Var(X) = (1-p)/p^2$.
The simulation uses `r format(params$N, big.mark = ",")` runs.

```{r item3-sim}
p <- params$p
N <- params$N
stopifnot(is.numeric(p), p > 0, p <= 1)          # validity check on p

one_search <- function(p) {
  k <- 1
  while (runif(1) >= p) k <- k + 1               # this site lacks the phrase: try the next
  k
}
X <- replicate(N, one_search(p))
```

## Simulated pdf, mean and variance

```{r item3-pdf}
pdf_sim <- table(factor(X, levels = 1:max(X))) / N
m_sim <- mean(X)
v_sim <- mean((X - m_sim)^2)

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Mean", "Variance"),
  Simulated = round(c(m_sim, v_sim), 4),
  Theory    = round(c(1 / p, (1 - p) / p^2), 4)
))

k_show <- 1:min(max(X), 12)
mids <- barplot(pdf_sim[k_show], col = "steelblue", xlab = "Number of searches X",
                ylab = "Relative frequency",
                main = sprintf("Simulated pdf of X (p = %g, N = %d)", p, N))
lines(mids, dgeom(k_show - 1, p), type = "b", pch = 19, col = "red")
legend("topright", c("Simulated", "Theoretical"), fill = c("steelblue", NA),
       border = c("black", NA), pch = c(NA, 19), col = c(NA, "red"), bty = "n")
```

## Conditional distribution after three unsuccessful searches

```{r item3-cond}
n0 <- 3
Xc <- X[X > n0]
Yc <- Xc - n0                                     # further searches still needed
m_c <- mean(Yc)
v_c <- mean((Yc - m_c)^2)

cat(sprintf("Runs with X > %d: %d of %d\n", n0, length(Xc), N))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Distribution = c("Complete set (X)", "Conditional (X - 3 | X > 3)"),
  Mean = round(c(m_sim, m_c), 4),
  Variance = round(c(v_sim, v_c), 4)
))

pdf_c <- table(factor(Yc, levels = 1:max(X))) / length(Yc)
cmp <- rbind(`Complete X` = as.numeric(pdf_sim[k_show]), `X-3 | X>3` = as.numeric(pdf_c[k_show]))
colnames(cmp) <- k_show
barplot(cmp, beside = TRUE, col = c("steelblue", "orange"), xlab = "Number of searches",
        ylab = "Relative frequency", main = "Complete vs conditional distribution",
        legend.text = TRUE, args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n"))
```

## Memoryless (Markov) property

```{r item3-markov}
res <- data.frame(
  Quantity  = c("(a) P(X=4 | X>3)", "    P(X=1)", "(b) P(X=5 | X>3)", "    P(X=2)"),
  Simulated = round(c(mean(X[X > 3] == 4), mean(X == 1), mean(X[X > 3] == 5), mean(X == 2)), 4),
  Theory    = round(c(dgeom(0, p), dgeom(0, p), dgeom(1, p), dgeom(1, p)), 4)
)
knitr::kable(res)
```

**Interpretation.**

- The simulated pdf decays geometrically and matches the theoretical Geometric($p$) mass
  function. The simulated mean and variance agree with $1/p$ and $(1-p)/p^2$ up to sampling error.
- After three unsuccessful searches, the number of *remaining* searches has essentially the same
  distribution, mean and variance as the original $X$, so the conditional and complete
  distributions are equivalent.
- The estimates satisfy $P(X=4 \mid X>3) \approx P(X=1)$ and $P(X=5 \mid X>3) \approx P(X=2)$.
  This is the memoryless property $P(X = n+k \mid X > n) = P(X = k)$: earlier failures do not
  change the chance of success on the next site, because the sites are independent.
- Conditional estimates are noisier because only about $(1-p)^3 N$ runs
  (`r round((1 - p)^3 * N)` expected) satisfy $X > 3$.
